md_description: This DAG describes a fluorescent staining and imaging workflow for cultured cell lines, including sample preparation, reagent-driven labeling with dyes and secondary antibodies, fluorescence image capture, and downstream computational analysis. It supports reproducible interpretation of protein expression and subcellular localization while retaining reagent provenance as experimental entities involved in the staining process.

cultured_cell_line_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the biological starting material, so I included intrinsic identity/provenance fields only: what cell line it is, where it came from, what donor/species context applies if relevant, and the culture-origin/state at collection. I excluded any preparation, fixation, permeabilization, staining, or imaging parameters because those belong to downstream Process/Capture nodes. I also avoided reagent, software, file, and analysis fields since those are outside this node’s semantic territory. No already_generated fields were provided, so there was no need to suppress overlaps with prior schema items.

md_schema.descr: Name of the cultured cell line used as the biological starting material at the root Entity node, e.g. HeLa, A549, U2OS. Use a standardized cell line name; this identifies what the sample is, not how it was handled.
Origin or repository/source of the cell line at the point the sample was established, e.g. ATCC, DSMZ, JCRB, laboratory stock. Record the source used to define sample provenance for reproducibility.
Species of origin for the cultured cell line at the Entity level, recorded as the biological source organism of the sample, e.g. Homo sapiens, Mus musculus.

Optional donor or patient identifier associated with the cell line if applicable and available in the experiment description; use a coded identifier rather than a personal name, e.g. donor_01. This field captures identity/provenance of the starting biological material.

Passage number of the cultured cell line when the starting sample was taken for fixation/staining, typically an integer such as 5-40 depending on the line. Record at the point the living culture was used, before any downstream process steps.

High-level biological state of the living culture at the time it entered the workflow, describing intrinsic sample status rather than treatment; for example adherent, suspension, or mixed. Do not use for process conditions such as confluency or media composition.

fix_cells.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only fixation protocol parameters and the operation’s agent/software-equivalent details insofar as they define how the transformation was performed. Specifically, I focused on chemical fixation conditions such as fixative identity, concentration, duration, temperature, and any quenching step because these determine preservation quality. I excluded sample identity fields (those belong to the Entity input/output nodes), downstream staining/imaging fields, and any raw file or analysis metadata. No already_generated fields were provided, so I did not need to suppress overlaps.

md_schema.descr: Name of the chemical fixative applied to the cultured cells during the fixation process, recorded at the time the process is performed; examples include paraformaldehyde, methanol, or glutaraldehyde. This describes the reagent used to transform the input cells, not the resulting sample.

Concentration of the fixative solution used during fixation, typically reported as percent w/v or v/v depending on reagent convention; example range 1-10 percent. Measure/record at the time fixation is performed.
Total time the cells were exposed to the fixative during the fixation step, recorded in minutes at the time of the process; typical range 1-60 minutes depending on reagent and protocol.
Temperature at which fixation was carried out, measured in degrees Celsius during the process; typical values include 4, 20-25, or 37 depending on protocol.

Name of the buffer or diluent used to prepare the fixative solution, recorded during the fixation process; examples include PBS or phosphate buffer. This captures the chemical environment used to perform the process.
Whether a quenching step was applied after fixation to neutralize residual fixative, recorded immediately after the fixation process; true if quenching was performed, false otherwise.

Operator- or protocol-level categorical assessment of how well the fixation preserved cellular morphology at the end of the process, based on immediate inspection before permeabilization; use standardized labels only.

fixed_cell_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the output biological material after fixation, so I included only intrinsic state-of-sample fields that describe what the fixed sample is and its preserved condition. I excluded process parameters such as fixative type, concentration, duration, and temperature because those belong to the upstream fix_cells Process. I also excluded downstream permeabilization, staining, capture, signal, and analysis fields because they are outside this entity’s semantic scope. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no overlap constraints to apply.

md_schema.descr: Current preservation state of the sample as a fixed cell culture at the entity level, recorded after completion of the fixation process and before permeabilization; values should indicate that fixation has occurred and is complete.

Qualitative indication of whether residual fixative is expected to remain in the fixed sample after fixation and before downstream washing/permeabilization; assess as a sample state attribute, not a protocol step.

Intrinsic sample-quality description of cellular morphology after fixation, assessed on the fixed cell sample before permeabilization or staining; use this to capture whether structures appear well preserved for downstream imaging.

Storage condition of the fixed cell sample between fixation and the next downstream step, recorded as a sample attribute when applicable; example values include 4 celsius refrigerated, frozen, or immediate_use.

Elapsed time in hours that the fixed sample was held after fixation before proceeding to the next step, recorded for the sample entity because it affects sample state between processes; typical range 0-72 hours.

permeabilize_cells.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only permeabilization protocol parameters that define how membranes were made permeable. I focused on permeabilization reagent identity and concentration, exposure time, temperature, and buffer because these are the controllable operation details that determine access of staining reagents to intracellular targets. I excluded sample-state fields, downstream staining reagent details, imaging/capture settings, and computed outputs because those belong to neighboring Entity, Entity, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so no overlap suppression was needed.

md_schema.descr: Name of the reagent used to permeabilize cell membranes during this process, recorded at the time permeabilization is performed; examples include Triton X-100, saponin, or digitonin.

Concentration of the permeabilization reagent used in the working solution, recorded during the process; typical values are low percent ranges such as 0.05-1.0 percent depending on reagent and protocol.
Total duration of the permeabilization step in minutes, measured from reagent addition to wash-out; typical range 1-30 minutes depending on membrane type and target accessibility.
Temperature at which permeabilization was performed, measured in degrees Celsius during the process; common values include 4, 20-25, or 37.

Name of the buffer used to prepare or carry the permeabilization reagent, recorded during the process; examples include PBS, TBS, or assay buffer. This describes the chemical conditions used for the operation.

Categorical operator selection describing the effective strength of membrane permeabilization achieved by the chosen reagent and conditions, assessed during method setup; use standardized labels only.

permeabilized_cell_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the state of the cell sample after permeabilization, so I included sample-state and readiness-for-next-step fields only. I focused on whether permeabilization is complete, whether intracellular access is sufficient for labeling, and any brief hold/storage state before staining. I excluded the upstream permeabilization protocol parameters because those belong to the process node, and I excluded staining reagent, imaging, and analysis fields because those are downstream. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no overlaps to avoid.

md_schema.descr: Current permeabilization state of the sample at the entity level, recorded after the permeabilize_cells process and before fluorescent staining; use to indicate whether membrane permeabilization has been completed.

Qualitative assessment of how accessible intracellular targets are in the permeabilized cell sample for downstream fluorescent dyes and antibodies, recorded immediately before staining; this is a sample property, not a process parameter.

Overall integrity of the cell membrane after permeabilization, assessed at the entity level before labeling; use to capture whether the membrane is sufficiently opened while cells remain structurally usable for imaging workflows.
Elapsed time in minutes between completion of permeabilization and initiation of fluorescent staining, recorded as a sample-state interval; typical range 0-240 minutes.

Storage condition of the permeabilized cell sample prior to downstream fluorescent labeling, recorded as a sample attribute; example values include immediate_use, 4 celsius refrigerated, or short_term_hold.

fluorescent_dye_reagents.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing one class of staining reagents, so I included only intrinsic reagent identity and provenance fields: dye name/identity, manufacturer or source, catalog number, batch or lot, stock concentration, solvent/formulation, and storage conditions. These are needed to document the reagent itself and support reproducible staining. I excluded protocol use details such as staining duration, incubation temperature, wash steps, and sample applicability because those belong to the staining Process node, not the reagent entity. I also excluded imaging, signal, and analysis fields, and there were no already_generated fields provided to constrain overlaps.

md_schema.descr: Primary name of the fluorescent dye reagent as an entity-level identifier, recorded exactly as supplied or commonly used in the experiment; examples include DAPI, FITC, Alexa Fluor 488, or Cy3.
Manufacturer, vendor, or repository supplying the dye reagent, recorded as part of reagent provenance; examples include Thermo Fisher Scientific, Sigma-Aldrich, or a named laboratory source.
Supplier catalog number for the fluorescent dye reagent, recorded as an identifier for the exact product used; use the vendor's item code format, e.g. A-12345.
Batch or lot number printed on the dye reagent container, captured to support traceability of reagent-specific variation; use the supplier lot format exactly when available, e.g. lot 1234567.

Stock concentration of the fluorescent dye reagent before dilution into the staining protocol, recorded as percent w/v, v/v, or mg/mL depending on supplier convention; typical dye stocks may be in the micromolar to milligram-per-milliliter range, but record the supplied stock value used in this experiment.
Solvent or commercial formulation in which the dye reagent is supplied or stored, recorded at the entity level; examples include DMSO, water, or buffered solution.

Storage condition for the fluorescent dye reagent prior to use, recorded as an intrinsic handling/provenance attribute of the reagent entity; examples include minus 20 celsius protected_from_light, 4 celsius, or room_temperature.

secondary_antibody_reagents.reasoning: I corrected the secondary_antibody_reagents Entity schema by removing field-name collisions with previously generated DAG fields. I kept only intrinsic reagent identity/provenance attributes that remain unique to this node and renamed the colliding provenance fields to more specific secondary-antibody-prefixed identifiers. I preserved reagent biology and conjugate details because they belong to this entity, and I excluded any process, capture, signal, or derivative information as before.

md_schema.descr: The antigen or protein target recognized by the secondary antibody reagent, recorded as the reagent identity at the entity level; examples include mouse IgG, rabbit IgG, or species-specific immunoglobulin subclasses when applicable.
Host species in which the secondary antibody was raised, recorded as part of reagent provenance; examples include goat, donkey, rabbit, or sheep.
Form of the secondary antibody reagent, indicating whether it is monoclonal, polyclonal, or recombinant; record the supplied reagent type rather than any staining outcome.
Fluorescent label conjugated to the secondary antibody reagent, recorded as an intrinsic reagent property used to enable imaging; examples include Alexa Fluor 488, Cy3, or FITC.
Manufacturer or vendor supplying the secondary antibody reagent, recorded for provenance and reproducibility; examples include Thermo Fisher Scientific, Jackson ImmunoResearch, or Abcam.

Supplier catalog number for this secondary antibody reagent, recorded as an exact product identifier; use the vendor item code format, e.g. ab12345 or 115-545-003. This field is specific to secondary antibodies to avoid collisions with other reagent entities.

Batch or lot number associated with this secondary antibody reagent, recorded for traceability of lot-specific performance differences; use the number exactly as printed on the reagent label or certificate of analysis. This field is specific to secondary antibodies to avoid collisions with other reagent entities.

Stock concentration of the secondary antibody reagent before dilution into the staining protocol, recorded in micrograms per milliliter at the time the reagent was prepared or received; typical range 0.1-10 ug/mL depending on supplier.

Storage condition of the secondary antibody reagent before use, recorded as a reagent attribute; examples include 4 celsius, minus 20 celsius, or protected_from_light refrigerated. This field is specific to secondary antibodies to avoid collisions with other reagent entities.

fluorescent_stain_cells.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the staining operation parameters that describe how fluorescent dyes and secondary antibodies were applied to the permeabilized cells. I avoided reagent identity/provenance fields that belong to the fluorescent_dye_reagents and secondary_antibody_reagents Entity nodes, and I excluded sample-state, imaging, signal, and analysis fields because they are outside the process scope. I also avoided the previously generated field names catalog_number, batch_lot_number, and storage_condition due to DAG-wide field-id collisions; instead I used non-overlapping process descriptors for the staining step.

md_schema.descr: Name or short identifier of the staining protocol used for this labeling step, recorded at the time the process is performed; examples include direct immunofluorescence, indirect immunofluorescence, or a lab-specific protocol code.

Total incubation time in minutes that the permeabilized cells were exposed to the fluorescent dyes and secondary antibodies during the staining process; typical range 5-240 minutes depending on protocol.
Temperature at which the staining incubation was carried out, measured in degrees Celsius during the process; common values include 4, 20-25, or 37.
Whether the staining reaction was protected from ambient light during incubation to preserve fluorophore integrity; record immediately during the process setup and execution.
Number of wash cycles performed after staining to remove unbound fluorescent dyes and secondary antibodies, recorded as a protocol parameter for the process; typical range 0-10.
Name of the buffer or diluent used during the staining incubation and washes, recorded as part of the process conditions; examples include PBS, TBS, or blocking buffer.
Whether a blocking step was performed before or during staining to reduce non-specific binding, recorded as a process attribute; true if blocking was used, false otherwise.

Immediate qualitative assessment of the staining outcome at the end of the process, before imaging, such as uniform labeling, weak signal, or high background; this is a process-level quality indicator rather than a derived measurement.

stained_cell_sample.reasoning: This node is an Entity representing the sample state after fluorescent labeling, so I included intrinsic post-staining attributes only: whether labeling is complete, which marker channels are present, whether the sample is ready for imaging, and brief hold/storage state before capture. I excluded staining protocol parameters and reagent provenance because those belong to the upstream staining Process and reagent Entity nodes. I also excluded capture, raw image, and analysis fields because they belong downstream. The previously flagged collisions on catalog_number, batch_lot_number, and storage_condition did not apply here because I avoided reagent-style field names and used sample-specific terms instead.

md_schema.descr: Current labeling state of the cell sample at the entity level, recorded after the fluorescent_stain_cells process and before imaging; use to indicate whether staining is complete.

List or description of fluorescent marker channels present in the stained cell sample at the entity level, recorded before capture; examples include DAPI, Alexa Fluor 488, and Cy3. Use this to describe the sample content rather than the staining protocol.

Qualitative assessment of how well the fluorescent signal is distributed across the stained sample before imaging, such as uniform, punctate, or heterogeneous; this is a sample-level property, not an image analysis result.
Elapsed time in minutes between completion of staining and start of imaging capture, recorded as a sample-state interval; typical range 0-360 minutes.
Storage condition of the stained cell sample prior to imaging, recorded as a sample attribute; examples include immediate_use, 4 celsius dark, or short_term_hold.

fluorescence_microscope_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the measurement session and instrument-configuration fields that define how the microscope acquisition was performed. I focused on microscope make/model/serial, objective and filter settings, illumination/excitation and emission configuration, detector/camera settings, exposure, and z-stack or channel acquisition mode because these are actively controlled at capture time and determine the raw images produced. I excluded sample properties, reagent provenance, file format/storage, and derived analysis fields because those belong to the input Entity, Signal output, or downstream Process/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided for this turn, but I also avoided reagent-style names like catalog_number, batch_lot_number, and storage_condition because those were previously flagged as collisions elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the fluorescence microscope used for image capture, recorded for the acquisition session; examples include Nikon, Zeiss, Leica, or Olympus.
Model name or number of the fluorescence microscope used during the capture session, recorded to identify the instrument configuration; example formats include Eclipse Ti2, Axio Observer 7, or DMi8.
Serial number of the fluorescence microscope used for capture, recorded exactly as on the instrument to uniquely identify the hardware instance; use the vendor serial format, e.g. SN123456.
Objective lens magnification selected for the acquisition session, recorded at capture time; common values include 20x, 40x, 60x, and 100x.
Numerical aperture of the objective lens used for image capture, recorded during the session; typical range 0.3-1.49 and it determines resolving power and light collection.
Name of the excitation light source or laser line used during capture, recorded as part of the instrument configuration; examples include LED 405 nm, laser 488 nm, or mercury lamp.
Emission filter set or bandpass used for fluorescence detection during capture, recorded at the time of acquisition; example values include DAPI, FITC, TRITC, or custom bandpass descriptors.
Detector type used to record the fluorescence signal during capture, recorded for the acquisition session; examples include sCMOS camera, CCD camera, PMT, or hybrid detector.
Per-frame exposure time in milliseconds used during image capture for each channel, recorded at acquisition time; typical range 1-5000 ms depending on sample brightness and detector sensitivity.
Number of fluorescence channels acquired in the capture session, recorded as an instrument/session setting; typical range 1-10 depending on the experiment design.
Whether a z-stack was acquired during fluorescence imaging capture, indicating three-dimensional acquisition rather than a single focal plane.

Effective pixel size in micrometers at the sample plane for the acquisition session, determined by microscope optics and camera settings; typical range 0.05-1.0 um and recorded to characterize image sampling.

raw_fluorescence_images.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact fields describing the image files themselves: file format, storage location, file size, image dimensions, channel count, bit depth, and basic technical quality indicators. I excluded microscope settings, sample properties, reagent provenance, and downstream preprocessing/analysis fields because those belong to the Capture node or later Process/Derivative nodes. I also avoided any duplicate field names already generated elsewhere in the DAG; in particular I did not use storage_condition, catalog_number, or batch_lot_number, which were flagged as collisions earlier. The fields below are therefore limited to the raw image artefact and its technical attributes.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw fluorescence image artefact produced by the microscope capture session, recorded for the raw data signal; examples include TIFF, CZI, OME-TIFF, ND2, or proprietary vendor formats.

Primary storage path, URI, or location of the raw fluorescence image file at rest, recorded for the signal artefact; examples include a filesystem path or object store URI. Use the path as archived for downstream retrieval.
Size of the raw fluorescence image file in bytes, measured after capture and archiving; typical range depends on image dimensions and can span 10^6 to 10^10 bytes for microscopy datasets.
Width of the raw image in pixels as recorded in the file metadata, describing the technical dimensions of the signal artefact; measured for each file or frame at ingestion.
Height of the raw image in pixels as recorded in the file metadata, describing the technical dimensions of the signal artefact; measured for each file or frame at ingestion.
Number of fluorescence channels stored in the raw image file, recorded from the signal artefact metadata; typical range 1-10 depending on acquisition design.
Bit depth of the raw image pixel intensities, recorded from the image file metadata; common values include 8, 12, 14, and 16 bits per pixel.

Whether or not the raw image file was stored with compression, recorded as a technical property of the signal artefact; if applicable this may describe lossless or lossy compression in the file metadata.
Technical quality indicator for the raw image file at the signal level, such as readable, corrupted, partial, or unknown, based on file integrity checks performed after acquisition.

image_preprocess.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only preprocessing operations and algorithmic settings used to transform raw fluorescence images into analysis-ready image data. I focused on software identity/version, correction methods, normalization, background subtraction, alignment/registration, and any filtering or noise-reduction choices because these define how the transformation was carried out. I excluded raw file properties, microscope capture settings, sample metadata, and downstream segmentation/quantification outputs because those belong to Signal, Capture, Entity, or later Derivative nodes. I also avoided fields already generated elsewhere and did not reuse colliding reagent-style identifiers such as catalog_number, batch_lot_number, or storage_condition.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to preprocess raw fluorescence images, recorded for the process step; examples include ImageJ, CellProfiler, Fiji, or a lab-specific pipeline.
Version of the preprocessing software or pipeline used during image correction, recorded at the time the process was run; use the exact version string such as 2.14.0 or 1.8.0.
Repository, package source, or code provenance for the preprocessing software or pipeline, recorded to support reproducibility; examples include GitHub URL, Git commit hash, or package registry name.
Method used to remove background signal from raw fluorescence images during preprocessing, recorded as a process parameter; examples include rolling_ball, flat_field, or none.
Radius in pixels used for background subtraction when a spatial rolling or local method is applied, recorded during preprocessing; typical range 1-500 pixels depending on image scale.
Whether flat-field or illumination correction was applied to compensate for spatial intensity nonuniformity during preprocessing.
Whether image registration or alignment was applied across channels, fields, or z-slices during preprocessing to correct spatial offsets.
Method used to reduce noise in the raw fluorescence images during preprocessing, recorded as an algorithmic choice; examples include gaussian, median, wavelet, or none.
Method used to normalize fluorescence intensities during preprocessing, recorded as a process parameter; examples include min_max, z_score, quantile, or none.
Immediate quality assessment of the preprocessed images at the end of the process, before segmentation; use standardized labels to describe whether correction and preparation succeeded.

preprocessed_image_data.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only the technical properties of the preprocessed image artefact itself: file format, storage location, dimensions, channel count, bit depth, and artifact/quality indicators after correction. I excluded the preprocessing algorithm and software settings because those belong to the upstream image_preprocess Process node, and I excluded segmentation, quantification, and interpretation fields because they belong downstream. I also avoided duplicate field names already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including reagent-style collisions such as catalog_number, batch_lot_number, and storage_condition, and used signal-specific terminology instead.

md_schema.descr: File format of the corrected and preprocessed image artefact, recorded for the signal produced by preprocessing; examples include TIFF, OME-TIFF, or HDF5-based image containers.
Storage path, URI, or archive location of the preprocessed image data file at rest, recorded for the signal artefact so it can be retrieved for downstream analysis.
Width of the preprocessed image in pixels as stored in the file metadata, measured after correction and before segmentation.
Height of the preprocessed image in pixels as stored in the file metadata, measured after correction and before segmentation.
Number of channels present in the preprocessed image data, recorded from the signal artefact metadata after preprocessing.
Bit depth of the preprocessed image pixel intensities, recorded from the file metadata; common values include 8, 12, 14, and 16 bits per pixel.
Technical indicator of whether preprocessing introduced obvious artifacts such as clipping, striping, or overcorrection, recorded for the signal artefact at the point of output from preprocessing.
Overall technical quality flag for the preprocessed image data, based on file integrity and visible correction success; this is a signal-level status, not a scientific interpretation.

segment_cells.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only segmentation algorithm and parameter fields that describe how preprocessed images were partitioned into cells and subcellular regions. I focused on software identity/version, segmentation method, model or threshold settings, input channel selection, and any post-processing choices because these define the computation performed. I excluded input image properties, mask output properties, and downstream quantification/interpretation fields because those belong to the Signal input, Derivative output, or later Process nodes. I also avoided previously generated or colliding field names such as catalog_number, batch_lot_number, and storage_condition, which are outside the segmentation process scope.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to segment preprocessed fluorescence images, recorded for the process step; examples include CellProfiler, ilastik, QuPath, or a lab-specific pipeline.
Version of the segmentation software or pipeline used during this process, recorded exactly as run; use the full version string such as 2.3.1 or 1.9.0.

Repository, package source, or code provenance for the segmentation software or pipeline, recorded to support reproducibility; examples include a GitHub URL, Git commit hash, or package registry entry.

Algorithmic method used to partition cells and subcellular regions in the preprocessed images, recorded as a process parameter; examples include thresholding, watershed, deep_learning, or template_matching.
Image channel or channels used as input for segmentation, recorded during the process; examples include DAPI, nuclear channel, membrane channel, or combined channels.

Numeric threshold used by threshold-based segmentation methods, recorded as the decision boundary applied to the preprocessed images; typical range depends on image scaling and may be 0-1 for normalized images or 0-65535 for 16-bit images.
Minimum object size in pixels retained by the segmentation process, recorded as a filtering parameter to suppress small debris or noise; typical range 1-10000 pixels depending on image scale.
Whether any post-segmentation cleanup or refinement was applied during the process, such as hole filling, object splitting, or smoothing.

Immediate quality assessment of the segmentation process outcome, recorded at the end of the process before downstream quantification; use standardized labels to describe whether the segmentation performed adequately.

cell_segmentation_masks.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result fields that describe the segmentation mask output itself: file format, storage location, mask dimensions, label/object counts, mask type, and output quality metrics. I excluded segmentation algorithm settings and software provenance because those belong to the upstream segment_cells Process node, and I excluded raw image properties because those belong to the input Signal node. I also avoided any already generated field names and did not reuse colliding reagent-style identifiers such as catalog_number, batch_lot_number, or storage_condition. The fields below are therefore limited to the derived mask artefact and its computed characteristics.

md_schema.descr: File format of the computed segmentation mask output, recorded for the derivative artefact; examples include TIFF, OME-TIFF, NPY, or HDF5.
Storage path, URI, or archive location of the segmentation mask file at rest, recorded for the derivative so it can be reused by downstream quantification or review.
Width of the segmentation mask in pixels, matching the corresponding image plane or stack after segmentation.
Height of the segmentation mask in pixels, matching the corresponding image plane or stack after segmentation.
Number of channels represented in the mask output, if the derivative is stored as multi-channel masks or layered label images; record the computed output structure.
Number of segmented cell or compartment objects encoded in the mask, recorded as a computed output summary from the derivative.
Type of segmentation representation produced by the derivative, such as binary mask, instance mask, or semantic label map; record the computed mask form.

Computed quality score for the segmentation masks, summarizing agreement, completeness, or confidence of the derivative output; record the score as produced by the segmentation workflow, typically on a 0-1 or 0-100 scale depending on implementation.

Categorical quality indicator for the segmentation mask output, based on computed or review-based assessment of the derivative artifact; use standardized labels to indicate whether the masks are suitable for downstream quantification.

quantify_expression_localization.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the computational analysis parameters and software provenance for quantifying protein expression and subcellular localization from preprocessed images and segmentation masks. I focused on analysis software identity/version/repository, the measurement strategy, normalization choices, per-cell or per-region aggregation mode, and immediate output quality because these describe how the computation was performed. I excluded raw image properties, mask file properties, and the resulting measurement table contents because those belong to the input Signal/Derivative nodes or the derivative output node. I also avoided reusing colliding field names such as catalog_number, batch_lot_number, and storage_condition, which are unrelated to this analysis step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or computational pipeline used to quantify protein expression and subcellular localization from images and masks, recorded for the process step; examples include CellProfiler Analyst, QuPath, ImageJ macros, or a lab-specific script.
Version of the analysis software or pipeline used during quantification, recorded exactly as run; use the full version string such as 2.4.1 or 1.53c.
Repository, package source, or code provenance for the analysis pipeline, recorded to support reproducibility; examples include GitHub URL, Git commit hash, or package registry entry.
Level at which expression and localization were quantified in the analysis step, recorded as a process parameter; examples include per_cell, per_compartment, or per_image.
Type of fluorescence-based expression metric computed during quantification, recorded as the analysis target; examples include mean_intensity, integrated_intensity, spot_count, or area_fraction.

Type of subcellular localization metric computed during quantification, recorded as the analysis target; examples include nucleus_to_cytoplasm_ratio, membrane_enrichment, puncta_count, or spatial_correlation.

Normalization strategy applied to fluorescence measurements during analysis, recorded as a process parameter; examples include no_normalization, background_subtracted, channel_normalized, or per_cell_normalized.
Whether and how segmentation masks were used as the reference for quantification, recorded during the analysis process; examples include direct_mask_mapping, region_of_interest, or none.

Immediate quality assessment of the quantification process outcome, recorded at the end of the process before downstream table generation; use standardized labels to indicate whether the computed measurements are reliable.

protein_quantification_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only fields describing the computed table artifact itself and its measurement content at a summary level: table format, storage location, row/column counts, scope of rows, and quality/completeness indicators. I excluded analysis software settings and quantification strategy because those belong to the upstream quantify_expression_localization Process node. I also excluded raw image and mask properties because those are input artefacts, not part of the table output. I avoided any previously generated field names and did not use colliding reagent-style names such as catalog_number, batch_lot_number, or storage_condition.

md_schema.descr: File format of the computed protein quantification table, recorded for the derivative artefact; examples include CSV, TSV, XLSX, Parquet, or JSON.
Storage path, URI, or archive location of the protein quantification table at rest, recorded so the derivative can be retrieved for downstream interpretation or export.
Number of rows in the computed protein quantification table, typically corresponding to cells, compartments, or image regions, recorded as a derivative summary statistic.
Number of columns in the computed protein quantification table, recorded as a structural summary of the derivative output; includes measurement and identifier fields present in the table.

Scope of the observations represented by the table rows, recorded as a derivative descriptor; use this to indicate whether rows correspond to single cells, subcellular compartments, fields of view, or mixed units.

Fraction or qualitative assessment of expected measurement entries present in the table, recorded for the derivative output to summarize missingness after quantification; if numeric, typical range is 0-1.

Categorical quality indicator for the computed table, based on integrity checks, missingness, and consistency of the derived measurements; use standardized labels to indicate suitability for downstream interpretation.

Whether the table includes derived summary statistics such as per-cell averages or region-level aggregates in addition to raw per-object measurements, recorded as a property of the derivative artifact.

joint_interpretation_analysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only the interpretive analysis parameters and software provenance for integrating quantitative outputs into biological conclusions. I focused on analysis software identity/version/repository, the interpretation framework, evidence integration strategy, confidence handling, and immediate interpretation quality because these describe how the inference was produced. I excluded raw image, mask, and quantification-table properties because those belong to upstream Signal/Derivative nodes, and I excluded the final report content because that belongs to the downstream derivative report node. I also avoided all previously generated field names and did not reuse colliding reagent-style identifiers such as catalog_number, batch_lot_number, or storage_condition.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software, statistical package, or analysis pipeline used to integrate quantitative outputs into biological interpretation, recorded for the process step; examples include R, Python notebooks, Cytoscape, or a lab-specific pipeline.

Version of the interpretation software or analysis environment used during the integration step, recorded exactly as run; use the full version string such as 4.3.1, 1.10.0, or a notebook revision identifier.
Repository, code source, or notebook provenance for the interpretation pipeline, recorded to support reproducibility; examples include GitHub URL, Git commit hash, or internal repository identifier.
Types of upstream outputs used as evidence in the interpretation step, recorded as process inputs; examples include quantification table, segmentation masks, and preprocessed image data.
Framework used to convert quantitative imaging outputs into biological conclusions, recorded at the process level; examples include rule_based, statistical_model, network_analysis, or expert_review.

Numeric threshold used to include or exclude candidate interactions or process inferences during the interpretation step, recorded as a process parameter; typical range is 0-1 for normalized confidence scores or an equivalent percent scale.
Whether a multiple-testing correction or analogous statistical control was applied during interpretation of many comparisons or interaction tests.

Immediate quality assessment of the interpretation process outcome, recorded at the end of the process before report generation; use standardized labels to indicate whether the biological inference appears robust.

biological_insight_report.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only fields describing the final report artifact and its computed content summary: report format, storage location, section count, summarized finding types, confidence summary, and output quality. I excluded interpretation software and inference parameters because those belong to the upstream joint_interpretation_analysis Process node. I also excluded raw measurements, masks, images, and table properties because those are upstream inputs or earlier derivatives. I avoided all previously generated field names and did not reuse colliding reagent-style identifiers such as catalog_number, batch_lot_number, or storage_condition.

md_schema.descr: File format of the final biological insight report, recorded for the derivative artefact; examples include PDF, HTML, DOCX, or JSON.
Storage path, URI, or archive location of the final report at rest, recorded so the derived interpretation can be retrieved and shared.

Number of major sections or subsections in the report, recorded as a structural summary of the derivative output; typical sections may include expression patterns, localization findings, and interaction insights.
Types of biological findings summarized in the report, recorded as a derivative content descriptor; examples include expression_pattern, subcellular_localization, and protein_interaction_inference.

Summary confidence level assigned to the report conclusions, recorded as a derivative-level quality or confidence indicator; use standardized labels to convey how strongly the interpretation is supported.

Assessment of whether the report includes all intended interpretation outputs for the experiment, recorded as a derivative completeness metric; use this to indicate whether key findings are present and integrated.

Overall quality flag for the final report derivative, based on integrity, completeness, and consistency of the summarized biological insights; use standardized labels to indicate downstream usability.
